small_guidance:
- The conv kernel iterates K=81 with full OC=16 broadcast; try larger BLOCK_S (512, 1024) and add autotune over BLOCK_S∈{256,512,1024} × num_warps∈{4,8} × num_stages∈{2,3} keyed on (N,S). Current BLOCK_S=256 is likely under-occupying.
- Hoist the weight load out of the spatial loop: load the full `[OC, IC*KD*KH*KW]` weight tile once into registers/SRAM per program (it's only 16×81=1296 floats) and reuse across all BLOCK_S positions, eliminating redundant `tl.load(w_ptr+...)` inside the IC/KD/KH/KW loops.
- Fuse the `* multiplier` and bias add into the conv epilogue (write `(acc+bias)*mult` directly), so the norm kernel's pass-1 only needs to read x (saves one global write/read of conv_out).
large_guidance:
- Recast conv3d as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC_tile, S_tile)` with `BLOCK_M=OC(16)`, `BLOCK_N=64–128` over output spatial, `BLOCK_K=27` (IC*KD or full 81) reduction. Use `tl.dot` on the inner GEMM instead of the current outer-product accumulate loop — this leverages tensor cores and is the main missing perf lever.
- Persist the entire `(C=16, S=12600)` conv output of one batch in the fused norm kernel by skipping the global write: produce conv tiles and feed them directly into the per-N reduction (single-pass online InstanceNorm using Welford so only one global read of x is needed). Requires merging conv + norm + clamp + max into one kernel per (N).
- Alternatively, since per-N S=12600 fits in ~800KB for fp32×16ch, run a persistent per-N kernel that holds the full (C,S) conv result in shared memory / registers after computing it, then does norm/clamp/max in-place without re-reading global memory.
